As a Firmware Release & Test Automation Engineer, you will own the final mile between embedded code development and physical deployment across our global fleet of connected devices. In this hybrid role, you sit at the intersection of build infrastructure, automated validation, and release governance. You won’t just run test suites or push buttons on a deployment train—you will architect the continuous integration pipelines, design Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) and Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) automation fixtures, define gatekeeping qualification criteria, and orchestrate safe, staged over-the-air (OTA) updates.

job.descriptionText:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Safeguards team plays a critical role in ensuring our AI systems are deployed safely, responsibly, and in line with our values.

As an Incident Manager, you will manage Safeguards incidents involving our AI systems from declaration through closure. You will assess severity, bring in the right people from Legal, Communications, Policy, Threat Intelligence, Security, Engineering, and research teams, keep leadership informed, and see follow-up work through. You will also oversee the Safeguards Enforcement on-call queue on a rotating basis, and help build and scale the incident response program, including runbooks, post-incident reviews, and automation of routine work.

Important context for this role: in this position you may be exposed to and engage with explicit content spanning a range of topics, including those of a violent, sexual, or psychologically disturbing nature. This role also includes after-hours and weekend incident coverage on a rotating basis.

Key responsibilities

- Serve as incident commander for Safeguards incidents from declaration through closure

- Assess what qualifies as an incident, propose severity, and coordinate responders across Legal, Communications, Policy, Threat Intelligence, Security, Engineering, and research teams

- Keep everyone working from the same facts by tracking input from each team, establishing what is known, what has changed, and what is still open, and sending regular updates that executives and partner teams rely on

- Make sure Legal, Communications, and Public Policy are consulted before decisions that need them, and coordinate any external notifications

- Run post-incident reviews, assign action items to named owners, and track them through closure

- Oversee the on-call queue during your rotation as the first responder for urgent requests and escalations to Safeguards Enforcement

- Triage each request, resolve what you can, route the rest to the owning team, and recognize when a request is the start of an incident

- Take part in after-hours and weekend incident coverage on a rotating basis

- Scope and deliver projects that improve the incident response program, such as on-call automation, incident readiness, and post-incident reviews and metrics

- Draft and maintain runbooks and standard operating procedures

- Work with Safeguards engineers to automate or reroute requests by writing the decision rules and testing the result

- Maintain the incident record and the metrics that show leadership how the program is performing

Minimum qualifications

- Experience running incidents or urgent escalations from start to finish in trust and safety, security, platform integrity, crisis management, or a comparable field, and readiness to lead high-severity incidents with support

- Hands-on experience with incidents where someone was abusing or misusing a product or platform, such as account compromise, fraud, or coordinated malicious activity

- Ability to make clear decisions under time pressure, record your reasoning, and recognize when a decision belongs to Legal, Policy, or leadership

- Ability to write short, accurate updates that an executive can act on and that hold up to legal and external scrutiny

- Experience coordinating people across many functions who do not report to you, securing their commitments, and following through on them

- Experience improving an operational process on your own initiative, and the ability to tell which steps need a person and which can be automated

- Willingness to do hands-on queue work as a regular part of the job, and to treat it as a source of information about what is breaking

- Ability to participate in after-hours and weekend incident coverage on a rotating basis

Preferred qualifications

- Experience joining an incident response function early and helping write runbooks and review processes

- Experience with incidents involving AI systems

- Experience with the enforcement steps that follow an incident, such as account actions, law enforcement referrals, or user and customer notifications

- Experience working with threat intelligence or security investigation teams during an incident

- Experience with regulatory or external incident reporting and disclosure

- Experience running an on-call rotation or support escalation queue, including setting and measuring response targets

- Experience using AI tools to automate triage, summaries, or routine decisions, with checks on quality

- Working knowledge of SQL or similar tools for analyzing incident and queue data

- Experience designing and facilitating tabletop exercises

- Genuine interest in AI safety and responsible technology development

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$245,000—$285,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. "Bring hands-on regulatory judgment to AI that runs the registered life of a product."

■ About Cheiron

Cheiron is building AI software for regulatory lifecycle management in the pharmaceutical industry, and we are working with our first pilot customers. The platform keeps track of what is registered in each market (the approved state, commitments and conditions, and the filings needed to keep registrations current) and, when a manufacturing or quality change is proposed, works out what it means in each market for review by qualified regulatory staff. It also drafts and checks regulatory documents. Customers keep their own regulatory records, and their qualified staff make the formal decisions; Cheiron supports that work.

■ About the Role

You will work alongside AI that produces first drafts, assessments and checks. Your judgment decides what is right, and your work makes the system better. You will be the hands-on global regulatory affairs expert on a growing Life Sciences team, responsible for regulatory correctness across the registered life of a product, from routine maintenance to the cases the guidelines do not settle.

You own the work for your assigned accounts within agreed scopes. Our Associate Director of Regulatory Affairs is the team's senior regulatory authority: you document hard cases, propose a position and escalate, and the Associate Director makes the final call. Expect roughly half your time on customer delivery and half on reusable content, validation and product improvement. At Senior Manager level you also structure ambiguous cross-functional work and lead difficult customer discussions; level reflects demonstrated scope and independence.

This role reports to the Head of Life Sciences. It is an individual contributor role with no direct reports.

■ What You'll Do

- Build the product with us. Work with Product and Engineering on how the platform handles registration maintenance, post-approval changes and regulatory documents. Define what a correct answer looks like, write reference cases and acceptance criteria, review outputs, and turn defects into specific issues with an acceptance check.

- Support customers. Onboard customer regulatory teams, prepare their account inputs, review outputs before delivery, answer their regulatory questions, and join customer meetings and on-site sessions. Explain clearly what is supported, what is conditional, and who needs to act.

- Bring hands-on regulatory expertise. Apply your experience with renewals, annual reports, commitments, variations and supplements, Module 3 content and health-authority responses to author and check the content the platform and our customers rely on.

- Work through the edge cases. Where guidance is silent, sources conflict or markets diverge, set out the reasoning, propose a position and bring it to the Associate Director, and capture that reasoning so the platform learns from it.

- Keep it current. Track guidance changes across markets and make sure the platform's rules and reference cases follow them.

■ What We're Looking For

- At least 5 years in regulatory affairs, including at least 3 years in post-approval lifecycle management, in pharma, biotech, a CDMO or a regulatory services company.

- Hands-on registration maintenance across markets: renewals, annual reports and tracking commitments and conditions. You can name the things that tend to slip.

- Post-approval filing experience in the US and EU (for example Prior Approval Supplements, CBE-30 and CBE-0 supplements and annual reports; EU Type IA, IB and II variations), and an understanding of how requirements and timelines differ in other markets.

- Personal authorship of regulatory CMC content: Module 3 sections, quality summaries, change justifications and contributions to health-authority responses. We will ask what you wrote, not only what you coordinated.

- Judgment on ambiguous cases: examples of resolving or escalating unclear or conflicting requirements, with the reasoning written down.

- A validation mindset: experience setting review standards, QC checks or acceptance criteria, and disciplined verification of technical text, including AI-generated drafts. Prior AI experience helps but is not required; no coding is required.

- Experience with at least one biologic or other complex product, and working knowledge of ICH Q12, Q5E, Q5C, Q1A(R2)/Q1E and Q2(R2)/Q14.

- Clear written and spoken English, and comfort discussing uncertainty directly with customers.

- A degree in pharmaceutical sciences, pharmacy, chemistry, biochemistry, biotechnology or a related field, or equivalent experience.

■ Nice to Have

- Post-approval filing beyond the US and EU (for example Japan, Korea, Canada or reliance markets), and health-authority interaction.

- Regulatory intelligence or regulatory innovation work, or AI-assisted regulatory workflows.

- CCDS and local label maintenance, artwork change control, or safety-driven label updates.

- Exposure to computerized-system validation (CSV or CSA).

- RAC; Veeva Vault RIM, eCTD or structured labeling (SPL, ePI).

- Experience at a multi-market company (biosimilar, generics or licensing), or with Korean- or Japanese-language regulatory documents.

■ Hiring Process

Application review > Head of Life Sciences > Working session > CEO > References and offer

- Application review with two short written questions (non-confidential examples only).

- A 30-minute conversation with our Head of Life Sciences.

- A 90-minute working session with the Head of Life Sciences and the Associate Director on a fictional product. You get a short source pack two business days ahead; reading it is the only preparation. You will work through a registration and change scenario that includes a commitment coming due and a point the guidance does not settle, write a short passage without generative AI, review an AI-generated draft, and explain next steps to a fictional customer. AI is optional elsewhere, and we provide access.

- A 30-minute conversation with our CEO.

- References (with your permission) and offer.

About 3 hours 15 minutes in total, with no take-home work. Exercise materials are fictional, and your work is used only for hiring. We aim to reach an offer within about three weeks.

■ Compensation and Terms

- The base salary range for this position is $150,000 – $185,000 at Manager level and $180,000 – $220,000 at Senior Manager level. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

- Part-time: pay is pro-rated from the full-time range based on agreed hours.

- Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, and 401(k); meal allowance (lunch, dinner); transportation support for early starts and late nights; in-office snack bar. Details in offer.

- Visa sponsorship available.

- Location: Bay Area (Los Altos), in person, with travel within the US to customer sites.

Cheiron is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability.

job.descriptionText:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Our Strategic Deals team originates, structures, negotiates, and closes the deals that secure the compute Anthropic uses to train and serve frontier AI systems. We work closely with engineering, infrastructure, finance, legal, product, and go-to-market teams to expand Anthropic's access to cloud capacity, silicon, networking, and the financing behind them.

We are hiring several Strategic Deals Leads focused on compute and infrastructure. In this role, you will source opportunities, design partnerships, and negotiate high-value agreements with some of the world's largest technology companies, and you will connect deal terms to structured finance solutions. Your work will directly shape how quickly and reliably Anthropic can bring new compute online.

Each hire will bring deep expertise in one or more of these areas while working across the broader infrastructure stack:

- Cloud compute: building and running a pipeline of capacity across established and emerging cloud providers, and structuring the financing that connects capacity commitments to their economics.
- Compute infrastructure: going deep into the silicon supply chain, structuring co-development and early-access deals with semiconductor and emerging hardware companies, and securing networking, backbone, and memory supply.
- Compute partnerships: owning multi-year partnerships with the largest cloud providers, where compute commitments, financing structures, model availability on partner platforms, marketplace and co-sell arrangements, and pricing and revenue-share constructs are negotiated together.

Key responsibilities

- Own deals end to end in your focus area, from opportunity identification and term sheet development through diligence, negotiation, internal approval, close, and post-close execution
- Lead negotiations for complex, high-value agreements with hyperscalers and other cloud providers, semiconductor and hardware suppliers, networking and memory vendors, data center operators, and emerging infrastructure companies
- Bring capital markets and financing thinking to every transaction, including vendor financing, equipment leasing, capacity prepayments, project finance, and credit and residual value guarantees
- Build financial models, term analyses, and commercial frameworks that compare supply options and give leadership a clear view of value, tradeoffs, and risk-adjusted outcomes
- Partner with engineering and infrastructure teams to understand future workload requirements and translate them into long-term supply strategies and commercially viable deal terms
- Build and own senior relationships with commercial, finance, product, and legal counterparts across the AI infrastructure ecosystem
- Drive internal alignment with legal, finance, engineering, product, and go-to-market teams on deal terms, risk parameters, and the approval path for large commitments
- Track market, technology, competitive, and financing developments across AI infrastructure, including supply constraints, and turn them into clear recommendations for senior leadership
- Represent Anthropic externally with corporate executives, investment banks, and infrastructure investors involved in our transactions

Minimum qualifications

- A track record of originating, structuring, negotiating, and closing complex, high-value technology, infrastructure, or capacity transactions as the principal and lead negotiator (not in a supporting or advisory capacity) and the ability to operate independently from day one
- Transactional experience in at least one focus area: cloud capacity or data center transactions, semiconductor and hardware supply (accelerators, CPU, memory, or networking, including backbone), or hyperscaler and cloud partnerships
- Working knowledge of how large infrastructure commitments are financed, such as vendor financing, take-or-pay obligations, equipment leasing, or project finance, and the ability to shape financing terms alongside commercial terms
- Financial modeling skills to build and pressure-test the economics of large infrastructure transactions
- Experience developing term sheets and negotiating definitive agreements alongside legal counsel
- Ability to work with technical teams and translate engineering requirements into deal structures, contract terms, and strategic business recommendations
- Experience negotiating agreements that combine infrastructure or capacity terms with commercial, product, or go-to-market terms, and an understanding of how those components interact
- Experience building partnerships and influencing senior stakeholders across internal and external organizations, including executive leadership

Preferred qualifications

- 8–10+ years of experience in strategic deals, corporate development, partnerships, investment banking, or business development at technology companies, hyperscalers, cloud providers, or financial institutions, with direct transactional ownership

- Direct experience working with or inside a hyperscaler on AI or cloud partnerships, including familiarity with model gardens, marketplaces, co-sell programs, and partner economics

- Experience managing multiple high-value transactions simultaneously at different stages of maturity and commercial development

- Comfort operating in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where market structures, provider economics, and partnership norms are still evolving

- A genuine interest in the future of AI infrastructure and in Anthropic's mission of building safe, beneficial AI

We're hiring for several roles on this team. Apply once, and we'll match you to the focus area that best fits your background.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$265,000—$325,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
